lesson_title: Distance vs Displacement: The Odometer and the Pigeon
hook_text: Run a whole lap of the track and physics scores your trip: zero. Correctly.
clip_script: Two instruments can measure one journey. The odometer counts every metre the wheels turn — that is distance: ground covered, whole route, no interest in direction. The pigeon ignores your route entirely: released where you finished, it flies straight back to where you began, and that flight is displacement — start to finish, direction attached. Walk 60 metres north, then 20 back south: odometer reads 80, the pigeon flies just 40. Now the extreme: run one full lap of the track and the odometer boasts 300 metres while the pigeon never leaves its perch — start and finish are the same spot. Displacement zero. The effort was real; the net change is nothing.
visual_style: Split screen: an odometer racking up digits against a pigeon on a straight dotted line; the lap punchline lands on the pigeon asleep on its perch beside a proud 300 m odometer.
pacing: Zero-claim hook, brisk two-instrument setup, lap punchline on the sleeping pigeon.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and split speed from velocity the same way.
